title: Missing Default derive on EmailAddress, AddressGroup — both have an obvious empty state
description: header_typed.rs:40 `EmailAddress` has `name: Option<String>` and `address: Option<String>`, both with the natural default `None`. header_typed.rs:55 `AddressGroup` has `name: Option<String>` (None) and `addresses: Vec<EmailAddress>` (empty). The rubric calls out 'missing Default where there is an obvious zero or empty state' as an idiom failure. Adding `#[derive(Default)]` is zero-cost, lets callers write `EmailAddress { address: Some(s), ..Default::default() }` and `AddressGroup { addresses, ..Default::default() }`, and works well in builder-like code. Less compelling for HeaderDateTime, where 'all zeros' would represent a date that the parser itself rejects in the year/month/day != 0 check (header_typed.rs:259), so Default::default() would build an invalid value — skip there. See related: MIME-o2c.9 (HeaderDateTime publicly constructable without validation).
close_reason: Type-definition cleanup batch on the typed header surface: (.4) added #[non_exhaustive] to EmailAddress and AddressGroup (HeaderDateTime was already done); (.5) dropped Copy from HeaderDateTime; (.26) dropped Copy from HeaderForm; (.18/.19/.20) added Display impls — RFC 5322 §3.4 mailbox/group form for EmailAddress/AddressGroup, RFC 3339 form for HeaderDateTime; (.34/.35) added Hash on EmailAddress/AddressGroup/HeaderDateTime/HeaderValueTyped; (.36) added Default on EmailAddress/AddressGroup; (.33) symmetric by-value internal signature on to_mail_parser/from_mail_parser. New public constructors EmailAddress::new and AddressGroup::new for callers blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. New tests cover Display, Hash, and TzSign.
